Firmware checkpoint — 2026-10-27: this preparation guide targets 23.0.1 on both Switch 1 and Switch 2 , while it is the latest firmware. Nintendo requires current firmware for the official save transfer. If a newer firmware has been released, stop before updating and get updated project guidance. A later update may change the future filesystem (FS) preparation path even if this Lua editor continues to run. On Switch 1, check that your CFW and bootloader support 23.0.1 before updating.
Accounts: add or use a user on each console linked online to the same Nintendo Account . These are the users whose game save will be transferred.
Version sources, checked 2026-10-27: Switch 1 , Switch 2 . See Nintendo's save-transfer requirements .
A modded/hacked Switch 1 is required. It must already be able to open the homebrew menu, where unofficial apps run. This guide starts from that point; it does not teach you how to hack a console.
The Switch 2 does not need to be modded. You use the hacked Switch 1 to restore the prepared save, then Nintendo's normal save-transfer feature moves that game's save to Switch 2. A stock Switch 1 or a Switch 2 alone cannot do this initial restore.
You do not need to build anything, write code, install Python or own a Pi. The editor save is already made for you.
Choose a transfer route before downloading the game:
You do not need the full game for nearby/local transfer. The demo works on both consoles. Local does not mean offline: both consoles still need an internet connection to Nintendo's servers and matching Nintendo Account users. The cloud route also needs Nintendo connectivity and the same account.
A demo save cannot be transferred to the full game. Keep the same edition throughout the restore and transfer. The full game can be launched on Switch 1 using Online License , as explained in step 1.C . Online License authorizes launching a purchased game; it is separate from the NSO cloud-backup service. See step 7 for the two transfer methods and compatibility evidence .
Your hacked Switch 1, including its microSD card and working homebrew menu.
A computer and a way to read the Switch 1's microSD card on it. A microSD card reader or SD adapter is enough. The file-copy steps below use Windows names.
The same Seedsow Lullaby edition installed on both consoles. The tested reference used in this guide is demo 1.0.0 obtained from the US eShop . There are also user-reported working cases for the Japanese demo , EU demo and US full game ; see compatibility notes for the distinction between reference testing and community reports.
The same Nintendo Account linked to the user you will use on each console.
Internet access on both consoles for the save-transfer step.
The matching account is for the save users and Nintendo's transfer process . It is not inherently required that this account downloaded the demo. Each selected user must be able to launch the installed software. When using Online License for the full game, only the purchasing Nintendo Account can launch it that way; use that account for the save user on both consoles.
Use sysNAND/sysMMC, not emuNAND/emuMMC, for this installation. All Switch 1 stages use the console's internal system storage. Stock is also sysNAND ; you only need to boot CFW on sysNAND to use JKSV . Download the game, link the account and transfer or upload the save in stock mode. The boot mode changes while the underlying saves stay the same:
An emuNAND/emuMMC is a separate system environment, usually on the SD card, with separate saves. Restoring into emuMMC does not put the editor into the stock sysNAND save you will transfer. Your bootloader's profile names may differ; choose CFW sysNAND/sysMMC for JKSV, then return to stock sysNAND/sysMMC . CFW on sysNAND is not ban-proof; an unbanned console is not a guarantee against a future ban.
Both consoles need Nintendo connectivity and account verification for the initial transfer. Blocking Nintendo servers beforehand can prevent it. Follow the firmware checkpoint above before accepting an update. This project cannot guarantee ongoing transfer availability. The editor itself needs no Nintendo connectivity. See Nintendo's requirements and compatibility notes .
If you already installed this editor, keep your existing save. Do not restore the starter over programs you want to keep.
These steps follow the nearby demo-to-demo route. If you own the full game and want to use it instead, install the full game on both consoles and follow step 1.C . Use the full game's own save and JKSV backup entry throughout; do not start with a demo save and expect either transfer method to convert it.
On Switch 2, make sure you can open the Seedsow Lullaby demo . If needed, obtain it through Nintendo eShop using an account with access. The download account need not be the user whose save will be transferred.
Add or use the intended save user and link it online to the same Nintendo Account you will use for that user's save on Switch 1.
Check that this user can open the demo, then close it.
1.B — Get the demo and make the first save on Switch 1
Boot Switch 1 into stock sysNAND/sysMMC, without CFW .
Download the same demo edition as on Switch 2 if needed. Highlight it on HOME and press + to see its version. This project tested 1.0.0 from the US eShop . Working cases have also been reported for the Japanese demo , EU demo and US full game , without exact version or feature details. These reports have not been independently reproduced by the maintainer. This guide follows the demo reference workflow.
Add or use the intended save user and link it online to the same Nintendo Account used for the receiving user on Switch 2.
On Switch 1, start the demo as the user whose save you will transfer, then choose New Game .
Hold R to skip through the opening until you reach normal dialogue.
Release R , then press ZL to open the save menu .
Choose an empty save slot ( slot 1 is fine), confirm Save , and wait for saving to finish. Opening the save menu alone does not create a save.
Press HOME , highlight the game, press X , and choose Close . Leave the game closed while working in JKSV.
Make at least one in-game save before opening JKSV. JKSV will only recognize the game for that user after a save has been made. Simply reaching the title screen or opening the save menu is not enough.
1.C — Full-game alternative: Online License on Switch 1
If you own the digital full game, you can launch it on your modded Switch 1 using Online License , without loading its virtual game card on Switch 1. The game must also be installed and playable as the full game on Switch 2 .
On Switch 1 in stock sysNAND/sysMMC , use a user linked to the Nintendo Account that purchased the full game . Link that same account to the intended receiving save user on Switch 2.
From HOME, select that user's icon, then User Settings > Online License Settings > Use Online License > On . Nintendo says this setting applies to the account across its consoles.
If the full game is not downloaded, open Virtual Game Cards , select the purchasing user and Seedsow, then Options > Download Data . This downloads the software without loading its virtual game card on this console.
Keep Switch 1 connected to the internet and launch the full game as the purchasing user . Do not run the account's digital games on both consoles simultaneously. Make an in-game save and close the game, as in step 1.B.
Use CFW on the same sysNAND only for JKSV backup/restore. Select the full-game save entry . Return to stock sysNAND and transfer that full-game save to Switch 2.
Online License changes how you access the purchased game, not its save edition. It does not convert a demo save into a full-game save. Check the compatibility notes before restoring to another edition: the prepared starter's metadata still targets the reference demo.
Nintendo's instructions: Online License , download without loading the virtual game card .
Download JKSV.nro from JKSV's official release . This is the save-manager app for your hacked Switch 1. It is not a Windows program, so do not try to open it on the computer.
Download Seedsow-Lua-Editor-Save.zip . This is the already-built editor save. Leave this file as a ZIP.
You only need the two files above for the initial installation. Seedsow-PC-Companion-and-Source-VERSION.zip is the optional computer app and developer tools; extract that on a computer if you need it later. Older releases call it seedsow-lua-editor-VERSION.zip . GitHub's Source code downloads are also developer files. The file you restore with JKSV is the Switch save ZIP .

Eject the SD card in Windows, remove it from the reader, and put it back into the powered-off Switch 1.

You have installed JKSV. You have not restored the editor save yet.
Boot Switch 1 into CFW sysNAND/sysMMC . This uses the same internal storage as step 1.B, with CFW loaded so homebrew can run. JKSV cannot run in stock mode. Do not switch to an emuMMC that has a separate save.
If the demo does not appear in JKSV, go back to step 1.B and make the first in-game save: New Game > hold R until normal dialogue > release R > ZL to open the save menu > choose an empty slot and save . Close the game, then reopen JKSV under that same user.
Open your Switch 1's homebrew menu . On many setups, opening Album from HOME opens it. Other setups use holding R while starting an installed game. Use the homebrew entry method your modded setup provides.
Select the user linked to the Nintendo Account you will use for transfer, then select the Seedsow Lullaby demo .
In the backup list, highlight New and press A . If it asks for a name, enter Before Lua Editor . If it names the backup automatically, note the name it gives you. Confirm and wait for it to finish.
Check that your backup appears in the list. This is your copy of the save from before installing the editor. Keep it.
Exit JKSV, then fully turn off Switch 1 again as described in step 3.
JKSV's buttons are shown at the bottom of its screen. In the current version, A on New creates a backup; Y restores a highlighted backup. JKSV's controls .
5. Copy the editor ZIP into the backup directory
Open the card's JKSV folder. Inside it, find the folder for Seedsow Lullaby . Its exact name can vary.
Open the card's JKSV folder. Inside it, find the folder for Seedsow Lullaby . Its exact name can vary.
Open that game's folder. You should see the backup you just made, named Before Lua Editor or the automatic name you noted. It may be a ZIP or a folder.

Leave your original backup in place. Eject the card in Windows, return it to the powered-off Switch 1, and boot back into CFW sysNAND/sysMMC for JKSV.

If you cannot find the game folder, search the SD card for the name of your new backup. The folder containing that backup is where the downloaded ZIP should go.
This replaces the current Seedsow save for the selected user. Confirm you have the backup from step 4 before continuing.
Highlight Seedsow-Lua-Editor-Save.zip in its backup list. JKSV may display the name without the .zip ending.
Press Y for Restore , then follow the on-screen confirmation. If it asks you to hold a button, keep holding it until the confirmation completes.
Wait until the restore finishes. Exit JKSV and fully turn off Switch 1.
Boot back into stock sysNAND/sysMMC, without CFW . The restored save is still on that same internal storage, ready for transfer.
The starter contains recovery slots 1-3 and examples in slots 4 and 5. It has portable JKSV restore metadata with personal account fields blanked, rather than someone else's account details.
Choose one method below. Both use Nintendo's services and the same Nintendo Account for the save user on each console. Return Switch 1 to stock sysMMC after the JKSV restore in step 6.
7.A — Nearby/local transfer: demo on both consoles
No full-game purchase or NSO membership is required. This is the beginner path used throughout the guide. It still requires internet access to Nintendo's servers on both consoles.
The same nearby method can also transfer a full-game save to the same full game . If following step 1.C, select the full-game entry instead of the demo.
Keep the consoles near each other, with both connected to the internet and the same Nintendo Account linked to the intended save user on each console. Switch 1 should now be in stock sysNAND/sysMMC , using the internal save that JKSV restored under CFW. Nintendo servers must be reachable.
On Switch 1 , open System Settings > Data Management > Transfer Your Save Data > Send Save Data to Another Console . Select the intended user and the Seedsow demo save.
On Switch 2 , open System Settings > Data Management > Transfer Your Save Data > Receive Save Data .
Check the user and game on the screens, then finish the transfer. If asked to overwrite an existing target save, only continue once anything you want to keep has been preserved.
This moves the selected save off Switch 1. It is Nintendo's individual-game save transfer, not the full system transfer used when setting up a new console. Availability depends on the installed software and current transfer support. Official transfer instructions .
7.B — NSO Save Data Cloud: full game on both consoles
Use the full game on both consoles : upload its editor save from Switch 1, then download it for the same full game on Switch 2. A demo save cannot be downloaded into the full game. Online License can let you launch the purchased full game on Switch 1 as described in step 1.C; it does not change this save rule.
You need an active Nintendo Switch Online membership , internet access and the same Nintendo Account for the save user on both consoles. Keep the original JKSV backup. Cloud uploads can replace an existing cloud backup, and downloads replace the target game's save; preserve anything you want to keep first.
Keep Seedsow closed during the cloud backup.
On Switch 1 , open System Settings > Data Management > Save Data Cloud . Select the intended user and the Seedsow full-game entry containing the restored editor save, then choose Back Up Save Data . Wait for the upload to finish and check its backup time before proceeding.
On Switch 2 , ensure the full game is installed and playable by the user linked to that same Nintendo Account. Close the game if it is open.
Open System Settings > Data Management > Save Data Cloud , select that user and the Seedsow full-game entry, then choose Download Save Data . Confirm that you are downloading the backup just uploaded from Switch 1.
Wait for the download to finish. The full-game save is now on Switch 2; continue to step 8.
Cloud backup copies the save through Nintendo's servers; it does not remove the source save like the nearby transfer does. Nintendo documents the general backup and Switch 2 download steps. Online License and cloud backup are separate features; neither converts the demo's save into the full game's save.
8. Stop here if you are only preparing for later
Once the save transfer or cloud download finishes, keep the game and its save on Switch 2. Loading the editor, running examples and testing reloads can wait until you want to use them.
You're set up. Everything else can wait. You do not need the Pi uploader, Python, coding knowledge or an editor update right now. Keep the game and its save, retain recovery slots 1-3, and keep your backup.
Ordinary editing, saving and running now happen on Switch 2 without a Nintendo connection . The optional Windows/Pi upload path is only a convenience, not a requirement for running Lua. You do not need Switch 1 for each new program. You can learn the console editor controls , add optional PC uploads , or install compatible later updates whenever you want.
